newsitem.title: UK: McDonnell Douglas indicated up $13 in London.
newsitem.headline: McDonnell Douglas indicated up $13 in London.

text.p: McDonnell Douglas Corp shares were indicated $13 higher at $65 in London on Monday, while Boeing Co shares climbed $5-1/2 to $102-1/4 after the two U.S. aerospace concerns announced plans to merge operations.
Boeing agreed to buy McDonnell Douglas for $13.3 billion.
"The market likes these mega-takeover stories. Wall Street will definitely open better," said one London broker.
At 1001 GMT, the March S&P 500 futures contract was up 1.45 points to 737.85 on Globex. That suggests the Dow should open 10 to 12 points higher, but London brokers look for bigger gains.
"Shares are firmer, bonds are up and we've got this takeover news," the broker said. "I think we could see the Dow up 15 to 20 points at the start."
Coca Cola Co shares added $1/4 to 48-1/8 after reports the soft drink giant's introduction of a new soda in the U.S. next month could be its biggest soft drink launch since diet Coke.
Coca Cola's new bright green drink will compete directly with Pepsi Co's Mountain Dew. Shares in Pepsi shed $1/8 to $29.
Technology shares bounced after Friday's broad decline. Shares in International Business Machines firmed $3/8 to $152-3/4.
Intel Corp shares, which lost $4-1/2 in New York on Friday, rebounded $1/2 to $132-7/8. Shares in Texas Instruments added $1/4 to $65-3/4, while shares in Digital Equipment rose $1/4 to $39-1/4.
Dealers said the market could be influenced later today by the November figures on capacity utilization and industrial production, due for release at 1415 GMT.
Yet few expect the Federal Reserve's Open Market Committee meeting, which starts Tuesday, to result in a change in monetary policy.
